speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, could you describe the frequency, consistency, and duration of your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To help narrow down the cause, do you experience any weight loss, fever, or blood in your stool?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you have any personal or family history of inflammatory bowel disease, and have you noticed any food triggers that worsen your symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_Ova_and_Parasites

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see the stool culture results are normal, which makes an infectious cause like Giardia less likely despite the camping history. To further evaluate for inflammatory bowel disease or microscopic colitis, I would like to check for inflammation markers.

REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the fecal calprotectin is normal, inflammatory bowel disease is unlikely, pointing more toward a functional disorder like IBS or microscopic colitis. Given the mucus and incomplete evacuation, I will order a colonoscopy to visualize the colon lining and rule out microscopic colitis or other structural issues.

REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal colonoscopy results rule out structural abnormalities and typical inflammatory bowel disease. Given the chronic diarrhea, mucus, relief with defecation, and exclusion of organic causes, I suspect Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D)
